analysis:
The PR changes docs/developer/build.md only. It adds guidance at head lines 180-192 on Swift 6.4.2 and SDK 27.2 weak-import behavior for Foundation's Date >= and <=. Pre-release macOS 27.2 builds may not export those symbols, so calls jump to address 0. The text tells developers to rewrite these comparisons with timeIntervalSince, and it names two checks: scripts/check-date-comparisons.py (Release Integrity in ci.yml) and scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py (the release lane of provider-release-build, run on built binaries).

No runtime code, authorization logic, key custody, attestation, WebSocket handling or encryption is modified. TB-002, TB-011 and T-052..T-058 are unaffected. The doc does not weaken any control and makes no new trust claim.

One security-adjacent point is that the documented guidance adds a build-time guard for expiry comparisons. Authorization and proof freshness checks (AssertionFreshness, RenewalInterval) rely on Date or time comparisons. A mis-compiled comparison jumping to address 0 could crash the provider, which is an availability issue, not a bypass. The scripts are described as best-effort: the source check has no types and can miss comparisons. The binary check is the backstop, and the doc says so accurately.

I did not see the scripts themselves or the workflow wiring, so the actual enforcement is not verified. The doc is not evidence that the checks exist or are enforced. Later passes should confirm that the claimed CI integration matches the workflow files if those are in the PR. No finding qualifies on the supplied evidence.
